staking_intelligence.analysis:
REWARD BEHAVIOR (new this run) is covered at the end of this section; the structural news is a correction.

THE DIRECT-NODE UNWIND DOES NOT EXIST. For three runs the model reported delegation TVL rising while total staked fell, attributed the ~215K difference to node operators leaving direct staking, and called it the largest unexplained flow it tracked. The residual is the wrong instrument. An unDelegate removes EGLD from a provider's `locked` figure immediately, but the EGLD stays inside the staking module for the 7-10 epoch unbonding period, so the residual (economics.staked minus summed provider locked) is a direct-node PLUS unbonding-pool measure. This week it flipped to +282,713, and a single wallet explains 229,865 of it: 149,585 unDelegated from p2p_org_ on 2026-08-15 and 80,279 from a second provider on 2026-08-14, both visible only as zero-value transactions with the amount encoded in the data field (the run #19 rule), both confirmed still unbonding via /accounts/{addr}/delegation with 6.1 and 7.1 days remaining. Corrected for in-flight unbonding, direct-node stake GREW +52,848 this week. The prior three weeks' readings - residual falling while delegation rose - are equally consistent with earlier unbondings COMPLETING, and the model has no basis to claim node operators were exiting. The protocol Staking SC cannot be cross-checked directly: every transaction-query variant returns HTTP 400.

DELEGATION TVL -236,435 TO 11,114,380 IS ALSO ONE WALLET. That same unwind is 97% of the decline; ex-it, delegation was -6,570 - flat. Per the run #16 single-entity rule this is a wallet event, not a market event. One provider did leave the active set entirely (locked 122,947 -> 0, seven users, and the second leg of the same wallet's unwind), the first >50K departure in tracking. Total staked itself ROSE +46,278 and the staked ratio +0.08pp to 47.46%.

TWO PROVIDERS SET A 100% SERVICE FEE, AND RUN #20's HEADLINE IS WITHDRAWN. egldstakingprovider - the provider run #20 celebrated for cutting 24% -> 15% as 'the first competitive repricing in twenty runs' - moved to 100%, taking its delegator APR from 7.82% to zero. procryptostaking, the incumbent run #19 named as the one that had NOT cut, moved 20% -> 100%. Both verified against /providers, /providers?identity= and /providers/{address}; both still run 50 nodes; the owner wallets are different, so this is two unrelated operators making the same move in the same week rather than one entity. Both continued to bleed: -33,182 EGLD and -13 delegators, -12,362 and -15. A 100% fee is a wind-down or a squeeze, not competition. The lesson for the model is narrower than it looks: fee arbitrage still describes where stake GOES, but a fee change is not evidence of a competitive market, and last week's reading inferred intent from a single parameter move.

The delegator response is worth its own sentence, because it is the strongest test participation inertia has faced. At a 100% fee a delegator earns literally nothing, and egldstakingprovider lost 26% of its book while its user count fell by just 13 of ~1,124. Capital moved; people did not. If a zero-yield signal cannot move retail, nothing inside the normal 0-20% fee range will.

THE THREE-WEEK 'DIRECT-NODE UNWIND' - carried for three runs as the largest unexplained structural flow tracked - IS A MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT. Run #20 recommendation #2 asked which node operators were unstaking. The answer is: probably none. The residual method (economics.staked minus the sum of provider locked) also moves when a DELEGATOR unDelegates, because the EGLD leaves provider 'locked' immediately but stays inside the staking module for the 7-10 epoch unbonding period. This week the residual flipped to +282,713 - and a single wallet (erd1daqlaezxx22rzy...) accounts for 229,865 of it: an unDelegate of 149,585 from p2p_org_ on 2026-08-15 and 80,279 from a second provider on 2026-08-14, both currently unbonding (6.1 and 7.1 days remaining, read from /accounts/{addr}/delegation). The runs #18-#20 readings, which showed the residual FALLING while delegation rose, are equally consistent with earlier unbondings COMPLETING (total staked falls, provider locked already reduced) rather than with node operators exiting. The unwind narrative is withdrawn.

BOTH HIGH-FEE INCUMBENTS SET THEIR SERVICE FEE TO 100%, ZEROING DELEGATOR APR - AND THIS CORRECTS RUN #20's HEADLINE. regime_shifts.description: A METHODOLOGICAL LEVEL CHANGE, and the most consequential result of this run. Circularity does not respect week boundaries: UPbit fed 319,000 into the desks in the Aug 3-10 window and took 130,000 back in the Aug 10-17 window, so each week's netting counts a leg whose mirror sits in the adjacent week. Summing weekly nets across the wave gives 326,924; netting the wave as one window gives 210,922, an overstatement of 55%. RULE: net over the WAVE (feed-to-drain), not the reporting week, and treat the weekly net one-way as an upper bound. The five-anchor backfilled series remains valid for weeks where feed and drain fell inside the same window - which is most of them, since circularity there measured 72-80%.

A three-run narrative is withdrawn. The 'direct-node unwind' (~215K over runs #18-#20, described in run #20 as 'the largest unexplained structural flow tracked') was measured as a residual that also absorbs delegation-layer unbonding in flight. This week that residual flipped to +282,713 and 229,865 of it is one wallet's unDelegate pair, still unbonding. Corrected, direct-node stake GREW +52,848. RULE: the staked-minus-delegated residual is a direct-node PLUS unbonding-pool measure; decompose it against /accounts/{addr}/delegation before attributing it to node operators. The protocol Staking SC itself is not queryable for transactions (HTTP 400 on every variant tried), so this is the only available route.

Run #20's 'first competitive fee cut in twenty runs' is withdrawn one week later. egldstakingprovider moved 15% -> 100% and procryptostaking 20% -> 100%, both zeroing delegator APR, both with 50 nodes still running, both under different owners. What looked like the delegation market finally responding to fee arbitrage was the start of two operators exiting or squeezing their books. The yield-arbitrage mechanism still describes where stake GOES (6 providers at APR >= 8.8% took +24,269 net, zero-fee providers +17,124), but it does not predict incumbent behaviour, and a fee change is not evidence of competition.

api_quirks: THE PROTOCOL STAKING SC IS NOT QUERYABLE FOR TRANSACTIONS. erd1qqqqqqqqqqqqqqqpqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqplllst77y4l returns a valid /accounts response (balance 14,514,270, matching economics.staked) but HTTP 400 on /accounts/{addr}/transactions in every variant tried - with and without status, with and without a direction filter, and on the global /transactions?receiver= form. Direct-node stake flows therefore cannot be traced through the staking contract at all; /accounts/{addr}/delegation on individual wallets is the only route to the unbonding pool.

/accounts/{addr}/delegation IS THE MISSING INSTRUMENT FOR THE STAKED-VS-DELEGATED RESIDUAL. It returns, per delegation contract, userActiveStake, userUnBondable and a userUndelegatedList with amounts and remaining seconds. This is what makes in-flight unbonding measurable and it is what shows the residual (economics.staked minus summed provider locked) to be a direct-node PLUS unbonding-pool figure rather than a direct-node figure.

A PROVIDER CAN REPORT serviceFee = 1.0 AND apr = 0. Two providers did this week (egldstakingprovider, procryptostaking), consistently across /providers, /providers?identity= and /providers/{address}. It is not an indexer artifact and it puts them outside every APR bucket, so bucket coverage must be reported against total delegated rather than assumed complete: 5 providers now hold 287,691 EGLD at 0% APR.

A PROVIDER THAT GOES TO locked = 0 DISAPPEARS FROM THE locked>0 WORKING SET, so its entire balance registers as a validator departure rather than a delegation outflow. One provider did this week (122,947 -> 0).
